ai.definition: Autonomous Quantitative Analysis is an advanced form of Financial AI that automates the process of generating financial models and reports directly from raw data, using machine learning techniques.
ai.howItWorks: This technology integrates live market feeds with large language models (LLMs) to analyze vast datasets and generate investment memos. The system processes raw financial data, performs complex quantitative analysis, and outputs detailed reports that can be used for decision-making in investment banking.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the need for efficient and accurate financial modeling and report generation, reducing the time and effort required by human analysts while ensuring high precision and consistency.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training machine learning models on large datasets. This includes data preprocessing, model selection, training, and validation stages.
ai.buildProcess: Building the system requires a combination of software development expertise in AI/ML, financial modeling, and data engineering. The process also involves integrating various third-party APIs for real-time market data.
ai.costDrivers: Costs are driven by the need for high-quality training data, powerful computational resources for model training, and continuous maintenance and updates to keep models accurate and up-to-date with market conditions.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is currently in early commercial stages but has significant potential for growth as more financial institutions adopt AI-driven solutions.
ai.regulation: Regulatory compliance is a critical factor, requiring adherence to data privacy laws and financial reporting standards. The system must be transparent and auditable to meet regulatory requirements.
ai.risks: Risks include model bias, data quality issues, and potential legal and ethical concerns related to automated decision-making in finance.
ai.profitability: Profitability is high due to the efficiency gains from automating complex financial tasks. However, initial investment costs can be substantial.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving model accuracy, expanding use cases beyond investment banking, and addressing regulatory challenges.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and high-performance computing requirements during training.

glossary.def: A type of machine learning model used for natural language processing tasks, capable of generating human-like text.
A document prepared by financial analysts that provides a summary and analysis of an investment opportunity or market condition.

subsystems.name: Data ingestion and normalisation
subsystems.role: pulls market prices, filings and reference data into one clean, queryable store.

subsystems.name: Quantitative modelling engine
subsystems.role: computes valuation, risk and screening metrics from the clean data.

subsystems.name: Language-model reasoning layer
subsystems.role: turns numbers and retrieved documents into readable analysis.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and scheduling
subsystems.role: runs the pipeline automatically when new data lands.
parts: event triggers such as earnings releases

subsystems.name: Verification and guardrails
subsystems.role: catches arithmetic, grounding and consistency errors before a human reads the output.

subsystems.name: Delivery and workflow integration
subsystems.role: puts the finished output where analysts actually work.

buildSteps.title: Define the analytical scope
buildSteps.detail: Fix which statements, metrics and model templates are in scope — a narrow, well-specified mandate is far easier to automate than open-ended research.

buildSteps.title: Build the data pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Connect to market-data and filing sources, standardise units and currencies, and store everything point-in-time so backtests cannot accidentally use data that was not yet published.

buildSteps.title: Encode the models as deterministic code
buildSteps.detail: Write the valuation and ratio maths as ordinary tested software rather than asking a language model to do arithmetic, and reconcile it against independently built spreadsheets.

buildSteps.title: Add retrieval and language generation
buildSteps.detail: Index filings, transcripts and prior notes so the model can quote them; give it tools that call the modelling engine so every figure comes from code, not from the model's memory.

buildSteps.title: Enforce grounding and traceability
buildSteps.detail: Require each number and claim to carry a source pointer, and configure the system to omit an item and flag it rather than guess when data is missing.

buildSteps.title: Build an evaluation harness
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a fixed set of analyst-written memos and filings with known answers, then measure numeric accuracy, citation correctness and error rate on every model or prompt change.

buildSteps.title: Insert human review gates
buildSteps.detail: Route drafts to an analyst for approval, log edits, and feed those corrections back into the evaluation set.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Watch for broken feeds, data drift and silent model updates; pin model versions and re-benchmark on a schedule.

prerequisites.why: structured filings and vendor price feeds are the raw material; without them nothing can be automated.

prerequisites.tech: Proven quantitative finance libraries and models
prerequisites.why: valuation and risk maths is well established and cheap to run deterministically.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with retrieval and tool use
prerequisites.why: they write fluently but are unreliable at arithmetic and prone to confident fabrication without grounding.

prerequisites.tech: Evaluation and audit tooling for AI output
prerequisites.why: financial text needs traceable provenance, and systematic scoring of generated analysis is still maturing.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory and internal control framework for automated research
prerequisites.why: research and personalised advice are regulated activities, so liability and review requirements shape what can be automated.

pathway.milestone: automated earnings summaries, screening and monitoring dashboards with an analyst in the loop
pathway.unlocks: large time savings on repetitive data gathering and first-pass screening.

pathway.milestone: agentic pipelines producing cited, auditable first-draft memos end to end
pathway.unlocks: analysts shift from writing to reviewing and challenging.

pathway.milestone: continuous monitoring that flags thesis-breaking changes in real time
pathway.unlocks: coverage of far more companies than a human team could track.

pathway.milestone: autonomous analysis for narrow, well-specified mandates under human supervision
pathway.unlocks: cheap, always-on analysis — bounded by model reliability, audit and regulatory limits rather than by computing power.
